import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np

# Load data
with open("/app/benchmark/source_data.json") as f:
    raw = json.load(f)

data = raw["streaming_rankings"]["data"]
platforms = raw["streaming_rankings"]["platforms"]

quarters = [d["quarter"] for d in data]
x = list(range(len(quarters)))

# Build rank arrays per platform
ranks = {}
for p in platforms:
    ranks[p] = [d[p] for d in data]

# Color palette — professional, distinguishable
colors = {
    "Netflix":            "#E50914",  # Netflix red
    "Amazon Prime Video": "#00A8E1",  # Prime blue
    "Spotify":            "#1DB954",  # Spotify green
    "Disney+":            "#113CCF",  # Disney+ deep blue
    "Apple TV+":          "#A2AAAD",  # Apple grey
    "HBO Max":            "#B01EFF",  # HBO purple
    "YouTube Premium":    "#FF0000",  # YouTube red — muted
    "Hulu":               "#1CE783",  # Hulu green
}

# Slightly desaturate YouTube red to avoid clashing with Netflix
colors["YouTube Premium"] = "#E06050"

# Line widths — emphasize Disney+ and Netflix
linewidths = {}
for p in platforms:
    if p == "Disney+":
        linewidths[p] = 4.0
    elif p == "Netflix":
        linewidths[p] = 3.5
    elif p in ("Amazon Prime Video", "Spotify"):
        linewidths[p] = 2.8
    else:
        linewidths[p] = 2.0

# Alpha — de-emphasize lower-tier slightly
alphas = {}
for p in platforms:
    if p in ("Disney+", "Netflix"):
        alphas[p] = 1.0
    elif p in ("Amazon Prime Video", "Spotify"):
        alphas[p] = 0.9
    else:
        alphas[p] = 0.65

# Z-order — Disney+ and Netflix on top
zorders = {}
for p in platforms:
    if p == "Disney+":
        zorders[p] = 10
    elif p == "Netflix":
        zorders[p] = 9
    elif p in ("Amazon Prime Video", "Spotify"):
        zorders[p] = 5
    else:
        zorders[p] = 3

# Plotting
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(22, 10))

fig.patch.set_facecolor("#FAFAFA")
ax.set_facecolor("#FAFAFA")

# Draw lines
for p in platforms:
    xs = []
    ys = []
    for i, r in enumerate(ranks[p]):
        if r is not None:
            xs.append(x[i])
            ys.append(r)
    ax.plot(xs, ys, color=colors[p], linewidth=linewidths[p], alpha=alphas[p],
            zorder=zorders[p], solid_capstyle="round")

    # Draw dots at each data point
    ax.scatter(xs, ys, color=colors[p], s=linewidths[p] * 12, alpha=alphas[p],
               zorder=zorders[p] + 1, edgecolors="white", linewidths=0.5)

# Label lines at start and end
label_offset_x_start = -0.6
label_offset_x_end = 0.6

for p in platforms:
    # Start label
    for i, r in enumerate(ranks[p]):
        if r is not None:
            ax.annotate(p, xy=(x[i], r), xytext=(x[i] + label_offset_x_start, r),
                        fontsize=8.5, fontweight="bold", color=colors[p],
                        ha="right", va="center", annotation_clip=False)
            break

    # End label
    last_i = None
    last_r = None
    for i in range(len(ranks[p]) - 1, -1, -1):
        if ranks[p][i] is not None:
            last_i = i
            last_r = ranks[p][i]
            break
    if last_i is not None:
        ax.annotate(p, xy=(x[last_i], last_r), xytext=(x[last_i] + label_offset_x_end, last_r),
                    fontsize=8.5, fontweight="bold", color=colors[p],
                    ha="left", va="center", annotation_clip=False)

# Y-axis: rank, inverted (1 at top)
ax.set_ylim(8.6, 0.4)
ax.set_yticks(range(1, 9))
ax.set_yticklabels([f"#{i}" for i in range(1, 9)], fontsize=10, color="#333333")

# X-axis
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(quarters, rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=9, color="#333333")

# Grid
ax.yaxis.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.3, color="#999999")
ax.xaxis.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.15, color="#999999")

# Spines
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)

ax.tick_params(axis="both", which="both", length=0)

# Title
ax.set_title("Streaming Platform Subscriber Rankings (Q1 2019 – Q1 2025)",
             fontsize=18, fontweight="bold", color="#1A1A2E", pad=20)

# Subtitle
ax.text(0.5, 1.02, "Quarterly rank position by global subscriber count  ·  Lower rank = more subscribers",
        transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=11, ha="center", color="#555555", style="italic")

# Y-axis label
ax.set_ylabel("Subscriber Rank", fontsize=12, color="#333333", labelpad=10)

# Annotation for Disney+ rapid ascent
# Find Disney+ launch point and peak point
disney_start_i = None
disney_start_r = None
for i, r in enumerate(ranks["Disney+"]):
    if r is not None:
        disney_start_i = i
        disney_start_r = r
        break

disney_best_i = None

for i, r in enumerate(ranks["Disney+"]):

            fontsize=9, color="#113CCF", fontstyle="italic",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="#113CCF", lw=1.5),
            ha="center", va="center",
            zorder=20,
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", facecolor="white", edgecolor="#113CCF", alpha=0.85))

# Annotation for Netflix sustained lead
ax.annotate("Netflix held #1\nfor 25 consecutive quarters",
            xy=(x[12], 1), xytext=(x[12], 1.7),
            fontsize=9, color="#E50914", fontstyle="italic",
            ha="center", va="center",
            zorder=20,
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", facecolor="white", edgecolor="#E50914", alpha=0.85))

# Annotation for mid-tier jostling
# Find a crossover area around Q2 2021-Q1 2022
mid_x = x[10]  # Q3 2021
ax.annotate("Mid-tier volatility:\n5th–8th ranks swap frequently",
            xy=(mid_x, 7), xytext=(mid_x + 4, 7.6),
            fontsize=9, color="#555555", fontstyle="italic",

            ha="center", va="center",
            zorder=20,
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", facecolor="white", edgecolor="#777777", alpha=0.85))

# Legend
handles = []

legend = ax.legend(handles=handles, loc="lower left", fontsize=9, ncol=4,
                   frameon=True, fancybox=True, framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="#CCCCCC")
legend.get_frame().set_facecolor("#FAFAFA")

# Add shaded band for mid-tier zone
ax.axhspan(4.5, 8.5, facecolor="#F0E6FF", alpha=0.25, zorder=0)
ax.text(x[-1] + 1.5, 6.5, "Mid-tier\nzone", fontsize=8, color="#888888",
        ha="center", va="center", fontstyle="italic", annotation_clip=False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.subplots_adjust(left=0.12, right=0.88, top=0.90, bottom=0.15)

plt.savefig("/app/output/result.png", dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight",
            facecolor=fig.get_facecolor(), edgecolor="none")
plt.close()
print("Chart saved to /app/output/result.png")
